phase: Phase 5: The rest of the inventory (after the look check) - step: duck (song-video prop, PM order 2026-11-17)
summary: PASS. The duck reads as a white duck at 128 px and in the 4 views: a flat orange bill, no comb, orange webbed feet, friendly eyes, rated G. The asset rating is 7.0 out of 10, which meets the bar of 7.0. The mech-check and the cutout-check pass at HEAD 7c95ea9a, both commits touch only the paths they name, and the 5 plan claims are true. The largest difference from the brief is the wings: they stand out from the body and read as small arms or fins, not as folded wings. All 10 findings are nonblocking.
nonblocking_findings: F1 [Nit] phase-acceptance: The wings stand out from the body. The brief asks for wings folded flat on the sides. This is the largest difference and the reason the rating stays at 7.0. The paddles stand about 3 cm out (assets/duck.ts:84-86, wingOut 0.03). In the front and back views they read as small flippers, in the S sprite as raised arms, and in the SW, NW, NE, and SE sprites as a fin at the back. They lie flat only in the side views (W, E). briefs/duck.md lines 89-90 say they read as folded wings at 1024 px; that is true only for the side view. Suggested change: lower wingOut toward 0 and turn the paddle so the tip lies along the flank, then check the front cutout.

F2 [Nit] phase-acceptance: The catch-light is large, and it is probably doubled in the textured build. The brief asks for a small catch-light. In the 1024 px front cutout the 0.004 m sphere projects to 8 px on an eye 19 px wide (left eye centre 482.5, 744.1). The white blob measures 9 x 10 px and sits about 3 px outward and 2.5 px above that centre. The kind also paints a glint (assets/parts/bird-kind.ts:345-358, sized by the glint option), and assets/duck.ts:78 keeps glint 1.9. The Known-differences text says the painted glint does not survive the coarse vertex-color mesh. That holds for --fast builds, not for the textured build that the deliverables use. I ran no --fast build, so I could not compare. The eyes still read as friendly, glossy eyes at 128 px (a white dot inside a dark dot). The owner fixed the sphere radius, so this is a note for the owner, not a maker fault.

F3 [Nit] phase-acceptance: The tail is faint and rough. The brief asks for a short upturned tail point. The tail-fan body (426 triangles) is a small tuft with a jagged, cut-paper edge (render.png side and back panels). It does not read in the S sprite, and it reads only as a small bump or grey curve in the other sprites. Suggested change: a larger tail with a smooth edge (tailPose scale above 0.7).

F4 [Nit] phase-acceptance: The wing edge contrast is low. The grey-white #dcd8cf against the white #f4f1ea separates the wing only by a soft shade edge in the renders. At 128 px the wing reads through the 1 px dark sprite outline, not through colour (sprites S and N). This matches the maker weak point.

F5 [Nit] phase-acceptance: The walk is small and stiff but usable. The feet step about 4 to 5 cm and alternate, the feet stay on the ground in all 8 frames, and the body bobs a little. There is no body roll, and the head stays still (stillNeck). In 3 of the 8 side frames (t=0.09, 0.44, 0.52) a soft dark shadow shows under the lower front corner of the wing. The three-quarter frames at t=0.44 and 0.52 show a dark patch at the top of the far leg. These are shadows in the strip renders, not holes. Rationale: this keeps the motion score at 3.5.

F6 [Nit] phase-acceptance: The jaw bone has no geometry. The build wrapper drops the kind beak and jawBeak bodies (assets/duck.ts:142-157), so the bill moves rigidly with the head. The fly, attack, hit, and death clips move a jaw that shows nothing. The idle and walk clips, the two that the brief names, are not affected. This matches the maker record.

F7 [Nit] phase-acceptance: The review card hides the head. scripts/review-cards.py:25 crops the lower half of render.png because it expects a reference row on top. The duck has no reference image, so row 1 of out/prop-cards/duck.png shows only feet and lower bodies. This is the same defect as F6 of the paint-pot acceptance. plan.md line 217 cites the card as evidence. A reviewer who reads only the card cannot judge the face, the bill, or the eyes. The fix belongs to the owner of the script and is outside this step.

F8 [Nit] phase-acceptance: The cutouts are older than the last source edit, and the maker log lists its commands in an order that differs from the file times. The cutouts were written at 22:04:45. assets/duck.ts changed at 22:07:27, and commit 4549de51 is at 22:07:37. The evidence commit 7c95ea9a is at 22:10:08; the final build files (22:10:48) and the card (22:11:00) are later than that commit. I compared the 2 delivered cutouts with the final GLB. A perspective projection of the final triangles (camera about 6 to 6.5 m away, at ground height) gives the same bounding box (front 381,699,643,1008; three-quarter 388,699,692,1008). Only 17 and 19 pixels differ by more than half alpha, and no residue survives a 1 px erosion. The 22:05:25 inspect and the final build both report 7,526 triangles. The silhouettes therefore match the final build. I could not compare the detail inside the silhouette (eye paint) without a second build. If the owner wants proof, run ./forge cutout and cutout-check again at the next HEAD.

F9 [Nit] phase-acceptance: Two statements in briefs/duck.md are loose. (a) Lines 73-76 say white is on body and tail-fan. The GLB has 8 bodies (legs, body, tail-fan, coverts, flight, bill, eye-glint, webs), and the wing bodies coverts and flight are not named. (b) Lines 89-90 say the wings read as folded at 1024 px (see F1). The wording is wrong and the results are right; no asset change is needed.

F10 [Info] phase-acceptance: The book holds two duck statements. Section 5 line 207 of forge-inventory.md at monorepo commit 9255c2711 says white in both weeks, with one render. An older note at line 249 says the duck is yellow in W2 and that Forge should not reuse one asset. The PM rule makes the section 5 table authoritative, so this is not a fail. The monorepo owner can remove the older note.
